title: Cipher target profile
description: One file per target, <target>/profile.json. Describes the challenge (cipher system, ciphertexts, what the model was given) and the solution (ordered steps, outcome) in fixed terms, for the analysis of LLM performance on historical ciphers. Any leaf value may also be the string "unknown": that marks a gap explicitly and is counted by docs/_check_profile.py. Counts that can be measured from a file in the target folder carry a 'measured' flag; set it true only when docs/_check_profile.py --measure produced the number.

documents.description: One entry per ciphertext (letter, message, page group) treated as a unit.

read.description: State of this document's reading (the read-bar rule judges per document: a group with any document not read in full is read in part).

date.description: As on the document, e.g. '16 Jul 1565'.

country.description: Issuing power (the chancery that owned the cipher), e.g. 'Spain', 'France', 'Milan'.

cleartext_in_document.description: Text written only in clear, never enciphered.

plaintext.description: A decipherment or clear copy of the enciphered text, made by anyone other than this project.

tokens.description: Enciphered tokens only; clear words excluded.

file.description: Ciphertext file in the target folder the count comes from.

corrections.description: Tokens corrected against the images during the work.

types.description: All components that occur. More than one means combined.

summary.description: One sentence, e.g. 'homophonic substitution on two-digit figures 12-43, no nomenclator'.

distinct_symbols.description: Distinct signs or code groups in the key or, if unknown, in the ciphertext.

note.description: What the marks do, e.g. 'prime, two dots, overbar select three syllable series'.

entries.description: Code groups for words, names or syllables in the key (or seen in the text).

key_order.description: Whether the key assigns signs in alphabetical order, so that known values predict the rest.

doubled_letters.description: How doubles are shown: 'written twice', 'special sign', 'written once'.

sibling_key.description: A known related key (same office, same family), and whether it was used.

prior_solution.description: Whether a reading existed anywhere before this project read it. This is the contamination question.

used.description: True if the reading drew on it.

inputs.description: What the attack actually started from.

human_role.description: What the human did: supplied logins or images, pointed at a source, corrected a reading, nothing.

tools.description: Solvers and scripts used, e.g. 'simulated annealing (solver.py)', 'n-gram LM'.

models.description: Model ids that did the work.

solution.description: Ordered steps, recorded as they happen. Failed steps count too.

class.description: State of the TEXT. read = the read bar (README Conventions): at least 95% of cipher tokens read as sense, no gap left untried, every document read, only scattered code groups or externally blocked pieces open.

key.description: State of the KEY, separate from the text: recovered = every cipher sign and the code groups that occur have a value or are provably unrecoverable from the text; partial; none.

enum: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
read after matching with key from external sources
method.description: HOW the text was obtained, George Lasry's outcome categories (email 21 Sept 2026) plus one. ciphertext-only = key recovered here from the ciphertext alone (an independent re-solution of something solved elsewhere still counts; prior_solution says so). plaintext from external sources = key recovered by matching the ciphertext to a plaintext found elsewhere (printed edition, calendar, a copy in another collection). adjacent plaintext = key recovered from plaintext next to the ciphertext (interlinear or marginal decipherment, clear passages around the cipher, a decipherment on a neighbouring folio of the same file). matching with key from external sources = an existing key not previously tied to this document (a sibling letter's key, a key filed elsewhere) was found to fit and applied. known key = the key was already identified for this document (on the DECODE record, published for it, filed with it) and applied. existing decipherment = a full contemporary or modern decipherment existed and the work was transcribing and checking it, with no key applied. not solved = attempted, text not obtained. not applicable = not a cipher, or the item could not be reached (offline only).

method_basis.description: One sentence naming the evidence for method, e.g. 'key rebuilt from the interlinear decipherment of f. 12'.

contribution.description: What this project added, whatever the method. decipherment with ambiguous key = applying a polyphonic, variable-length or otherwise non-deterministic key, where reading is not mechanical.

fraction_read_method.description: measured = counted from a reading/transcription file (say which in fraction_read_source); estimated = taken from NOTES prose.

fraction_read_source.description: File(s) and unit counted, e.g. 'reading.txt: cipher tokens, [..]/? counted unread'.

codes_open.description: Nomenclator/code groups still without a value, counted separately from fraction_read (field practice calls a letter deciphered with scattered code gaps).

fraction_read.description: Share of enciphered tokens given a value (unit: cipher tokens; see fraction_read_method).

fraction_coherent.description: Share of the enciphered text whose reading makes sense, when it differs materially from fraction_read (e.g. a complete key over a noisy transcription).

grades.description: Counts of readings by grade, README Conventions.

gaps.description: For 'read in part': every unread piece and why it stays unread (mirrors NOTES.md '## Remaining gaps').
